angleRead.name: Lila Mezran
angleRead.text: I'm standing at the corner of Webster and 8th, watching the lunch crowd move between the bakery and the pharmacy. The numbers say Chinatown is carrying more sick residents than any other neighborhood — 137, down three from last cycle but still the highest in the city. Six percent of the neighborhood, which puts us at or over the watch bar. But here's what doesn't line up: only three admissions from Chinatown this cycle, six people in care at the close. The illness is here, but the hospital trail is thin. I want to walk the blocks between the clinics and the residential hotels, talk to people who live here — Jax Caldera, the freelance accountability writer who knows this neighborhood's paperw
